references.text: Jephthah refers to Israel's history when they wandered through the wilderness and did not take land from Moab or Ammon, but went around their territory.
Jephthah points out that Israel took the land from the Amorites, not from Moab or Ammon, when they captured Heshbon and the surrounding areas.
God commanded Israel not to attack Moab, because He had given Ar to Lot's descendants as a possession.
God commanded Israel not to attack the Ammonites, because He had given the land to Lot's descendants as a possession.
Similar diplomatic communication where Israel sends messengers to a king to explain their situation and intentions.
The context in which Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the Ammonites to negotiate, and the king responds with his claim to the land.
